title.narrative: Policy Dialogue on Legislative Reform to Improve Land Governance and Secure Tenure Rights by Registering and Resolving Land Claims for vulnerable IDPs in Iraq.

description.narrative:
The goal of the project is to initiate policy dialogues on land legal framework, improve land governance by analyzing urban law framework sensitivity to HLP and facilitating slum upgrading processes, build local capacity on HLP and contribute to increasing the security of tenure and protection of HLP rights for all, including IDPs and returnees in war affected governorates. The objective of the project is to “Facilitate the policy dialogue on the land legal framework reform to improve land governance and enhance the security of tenure of IDPs and returnees by addressing, supporting, and protecting their HLP rights”. In addition to policy dialogues and enhancing the security of tenure, the proposed project will contribute to the overall goal of the complementary and joint efforts with other partners, to support other components related to digital registration of HLP rights: create a legal background for the ICT-based solution, assist the digitization phase, automate the property registration systems, conduct study visits, and support capacity building on cadasters aiming to digitize property records, and develop the issuance of digital title deeds with a new GIS system, improve land governance and the climate of businesses and investors in Iraq, and improve the living conditions of Iraqis, including IDPs.
1) Through the policy dialogue approach, the legislative reform will improve the land governance system in Iraq and set in motion effective, digitized land management in the real estate registration offices with digitized property records and electronic registries of transactions. It will significantly enhance and guarantee ownership and increase the security of tenure, improve access to HLP rights, and obtain HLP documentation though a digitized system . This in turn will improve living conditions, reduce land disputes, improve urban planning, increase the responsibility and control over land, and achieve durable solutions. All in all, the reform of the HLP legislation/legal framework will contribute directly to peacebuilding and reconciliation efforts and increase chances for investment and economic development in post-war Iraq. Participation in the adaptation of the HLP legislation/legal framework will enable all relevant counterparts, stakeholders, including civil society and relevant I/NGOs, to raise the issues of the land governance and HLP rights, share perspectives on how IDPs and returnees are negatively affected by outdated laws and long bureaucratic processes to access their HLP rights, obtain HLP documentation and find common, practical and policy solutions to accelerate and simplify the process to register their HLP rights or obtain their ownership documentation. Further, it will enable the future deployment of a modern Land Management System for Iraq, resulting in secure HLP rights and tenure security. Through this project, UN-Habitat aims also to initiate policy dialogues on the reform of legislation/legal framework with the objective to improve land governance by establishing an inclusive and effective land management system and increase the security of tenure for all Iraqis, including IDPs, returnees, and all Iraqis who face challenges to accessing HLP rights. The improvement of land governance, revision of the land legal framework, and building capacity at the local level on land management will contribute to increasing the security of tenure and protection of HLP rights for all, including IDPs and returnees in the targeted governorates. For the review of the Iraqi legal framework, the project will be applied in Baghdad and piloted in Anbar, Ninewa, Erbil governorates and Sinjar district, where most of the IDPs are affected by violations or face barriers to accessing their HLP rights. Lastly, under the outcome 1, through this intervention, the project will support the government in developing a new environment for improved land management and capacity building for government and cadastral officials to better manage HLP rights. Good land governance will reduce poverty, increase food security, and improve cases of gender inequality concerning land rights for all IDPs and returnees, especially in war-affected governorates.
2)To improve the security of tenure for the IDPs, UN-Habitat will register land claims and issuing land occupancy certificates by using STDM. The HLP land occupancy certificates will be issued to households who had no HLP documentation until now, accompanied by advocacy efforts with official institutions; this sets the basis for an institutional response in favor of HLP rights of vulnerable populations at the national level. The Social tenure Domain Model (STDM) will be used to improve land tenure, which will allow the management of informal and alternative tenure documents and administrative, and spatial data.
